Here is a clearer, more professional, and well-structured version of the email with a neutral, business-appropriate tone and no em dashes:

:::writing{id="83421" variant="email" subject="Stripe Receipt and February Billing Clarification"}
Good morning Sam,

I contacted Stripe regarding this matter, and they provided the following receipt for reference:
https://pay.stripe.com/receipts/invoices/CAcQARoXChVhY2N0XzFSUktCdkFVaE1XenVsNHYolqj3zAYyBr-fif8ubzosFtl6GkpSJfG3cJGNERSnHLRIqKwPPEM8T5IRxeYk_KJEF_ENRAQ3lItLgXc?s=ap

Please let me know if there is anything further I can provide to assist.

To clarify the billing details: you were not ultimately charged the $1,500 fee, and therefore no retraction of a refund is being requested. The $1,500 was originally intended to be billed in February as part of a transition to hourly manual work. However, after the charge was mistakenly refunded by my assistant, I chose not to rebill it. Instead, I informed Tracy that it would be more appropriate for your team to cover that expense directly so you would retain full control of the associated account. Access was provided to both you and Tracy for this reason, particularly because several contacts we reached out to asked whether she was involved with AmSpa.

Regarding the February billing adjustment, the reason we reduced the retainer from $3,500 to $1,500 was to transition to a different, more cost-effective approach for continuing outreach. You will not be billed for a new February invoice.

As agreed, we had a 90-day period to fulfill our guarantee, which began on December 13 following the initial onboarding period. Since that 90-day window has concluded and we did not yet reach the 15 qualified calls, I will continue working at no cost until the guarantee is fully met.

Please let me know if you would like to discuss any of this further.

Best regards,  
Bethany
:::

If you want this tightened further for legal review or softened for relationship management, I can provide an alternate version.
